deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Five points A, B, C, D, E in the plane. A and D are expressed as affine (barycentric) combinations of the reference triangle B, C, E, with coefficients summing to 1:
  A = pB - qC + (1-p+q)E,
  D = -rB + sC + (1+r-s)E.
The page then computes, in the same barycentric frame, the five intersection points of the diagonals of the pentagon ABCDE. These are the five vertices a, b, c, d, e of the inner pentagon of the pentagram.

Upper block (results). Each point is multiplied by the sum of its coefficients; a dot marks an empty slot.
  (1+r)a = sC + (1+r-s)E
  (1+q)d = pB + (1-p+q)E
  (p+r)b = (ps-qr)C + (p+r-ps+qr)E
  (q+s)c = (ps-qr)B + (q+s-ps+qr)E
  (1+q+r-ps+qr)e = p(1+r-s)B + s(1-p+q)C + (1-p+q)(1+r-s)E

Right-hand block (justification). Each point is shown to lie on two diagonals by writing it as a combination of two vertices.
- d: A + qC = (1+q)d. Substitute A to get pB + (1-p+q)E. So d lies on both AC and BE, i.e. d = AC ∩ BE.
- a: rB + D = (1+r)a. The B terms cancel, giving sC + (1+r-s)E. So a = BD ∩ CE.
- c: sA + qD = (q+s)c. The C terms cancel (-sq + qs = 0), giving (ps-qr)B + (q+s-ps+qr)E. So c = AD ∩ BE.
- b: rA + pD = (p+r)b. The B terms cancel, giving (ps-qr)C + (p+r-ps+qr)E. So b = AD ∩ CE.
- e (first representation): (1+r-s)A + (q+s-ps+qr)C = (1+q+r-ps+qr)e. The C coefficient becomes -q(1+r-s) + q + s - ps + qr = s(1-p+q). So e lies on AC.
- e (second representation): (p+r-ps+qr)B + (1-p+q)D = (1+q+r-ps+qr)e. The B coefficient becomes p+r-ps+qr - r(1-p+q) = p(1+r-s). So e lies on BD.
- Conclusion: e = AC ∩ BD.
- [My check] Coefficient sums: (1-p+q)(1+r-s) + p(1+r-s) + s(1-p+q) = 1 + q + r - ps + qr.

Bottom block (recap of the elimination). It restates sA + qD and rA + pD. It then eliminates E between A and D:
  (1+r-s)A - (1-p+q)D = (p+r-ps+qr)B - (q+s-ps+qr)C.
This is the point AD ∩ BC, written unnormalized. Both coefficient sums equal p - q + r - s.

Left margin. The fragment ((p+r)/(ps-qr))·b + ((q+s)/(ps-qr))·c appears. Combining the b and c equations gives
  (p+r)b + (q+s)c = (ps-qr)(B+C) + (p+q+r+s-2ps+2qr)E,
so this is presumably a step toward expressing B and C (or ratios on the line AD) through b and c. Its exact purpose is unsure.

Purpose. The five points are e = AC∩BD, a = BD∩CE, b = CE∩DA, c = DA∩EB, d = EB∩AC: the intersections of consecutive diagonals, i.e. the inner pentagon of the pentagram. The next page computes triangle areas by determinants, with parameters k, l, m, n. It also contains the relation ωω − ∫ω + ∫' = 0, i.e. ω² − (Σ)ω + (Σ of adjacent products) = 0. That is Gauss's quadratic for the area ω of a pentagon in terms of the five 'vertex triangles' (ω = b + d + a/(ω − b − d) etc.). So this page is coordinate groundwork for Gauss's pentagon-area investigations, apparently comparing the outer pentagon with the pentagram's inner pentagon. The envelope is addressed to 'Hofrath Gauss hierselbst', so it dates after 1816.
errors: In the second representation of e, the manuscript reads '+(p+r+ps-qr)B + (1-p+q)D = (1+q+r-ps+qr)e'. Consistency of coefficient sums and of the B-coefficient requires (p+r-ps+qr)B. The sign of the ps-qr term is slipped. The same quantity is written correctly as (p+r-ps+qr) in the bottom line.
Two minus signs in the bottom lines ('p+r ● ps+qr') are obscured by ink blots. Algebra confirms they are minus signs. These are legibility issues, not mathematical errors.
All other identities on the page check out exactly.

results.what: Barycentric/affine coordinates (w.r.t. triangle BCE) of the five intersection points of consecutive diagonals of a pentagon ABCDE (inner pentagon of the pentagram), obtained by eliminating one reference vertex between pairs of points
results.modern_name: Intersection of lines in barycentric (affine) coordinates; Möbius-style barycentric calculus
results.usually_credited_to: Barycentric calculus: Möbius (1827); the technique itself is elementary

results.what: Preparatory computation for the pentagon area relation ω² − (Σ triangles)ω + Σ(adjacent products) = 0 (context from the following page)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (communicated c. 1823, printed in Werke IV)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine affine/barycentric algebra locating the diagonal intersection points of a pentagon. It is evidently scratch work for Gauss's known pentagon-area investigations, which are already attributed to him. The fact that he used barycentric-type point combinations before or alongside Möbius is mildly interesting but not novel.

transcription_corrections: Line '+(p+r+ps-qr)B + (1-p+q)D = (1+q+r-ps+qr)e': the manuscript indeed appears to read '+ps-qr', but this is Gauss's slip; mathematically it should be (p+r-ps+qr)B.
Bottom lines: the blotted symbol in '(p+r ● ps+qr)' is a minus sign, i.e. (p+r-ps+qr), in both occurrences.
Upper block: the dots ('·') are placeholders for vanishing B or C coefficients, not multiplication signs.
